summary: Keith Dowman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Anagarika Munindra. In 1973, he held a post at Sonoma State University.

Keiya Noguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He taught as a lecturer and professor at Shuchiin University and served as a lecturer and institute director at Taisho University.

Kelsang Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Chambaling, Tashi Lhunpo, Ngamring Chöde, and Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche, taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre, and founded the New Kadampa Tradition.

Kelsey Alise Seymour specializes in Sinology and Japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair and was a Visiting Predoctoral Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science from 2017 to 2018.
Kemo Jin was an Indologist, Sinologist, and linguist. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University from 1941 to 1945 and became Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University in 1948.

Ken McLeod works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an M.Sc. at the University of British Columbia, studied with Kalu Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa, served as resident teacher at Kagyu Dongak Chuling, and founded Unfettered Mind.
Kendall Marchman specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Mario Poceski and earned his PhD at the University of Florida in 2015.

Kengo Harimoto specializes in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Nagasaki, Kyushu, and the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass, he held posts at institutions including Hamburg, Leiden, Mahidol, and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".
Kenichi Kuranishi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as an associate professor at Taisho University and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg.
Kenji Ishii is a religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1974 to 1984 and held a post at Kokugakuin University from circa 1987 to 2020.
Kenji Kinugawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1971 to 1980 under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Kenji Matsuo is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1973 to 1982 and held a post at Yamagata University from circa 1988 to 2020.
Kenji Shimada was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and history. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1938 to 1941 and later held a research post there from circa 1949 to 1981.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University and under doctoral supervisors Diwakar Acharya and Yuko Yokochi. He held posts at Kyoto University and as a fellow at the University of Naples Federico II.
Kenji Watanabe specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held an assistant post at the University of Tokyo from around 1977 to 1979 and studied under Jozef Deleu from circa 1979 to 1982.
Kenjiu Kasawara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, where he was taught by Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Kenjuro Yanagida was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida. He held a post at Hirosaki University from around 1950 to 1952.

Kenkai Naganuma was a historian and Japanologist. He held posts at Kyushu University from circa 1925 to 1946, where he was professor emeritus, and subsequently at Kurume University from circa 1950 to 1963.
Kennard Lipman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther and worked as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University.
